00001| # Dogfooding the JavaScript Formal AI on agentic coding tasks (PR #1188)
00002| 
00003| The JavaScript root of Formal AI runs from source (`node js/server/main.mjs
00004| --agent-mode`), with no Rust build, so it is the fast loop for making Formal
00005| AI do agentic coding itself. This ledger records every task it was given,
00006| what it did, and the fix when it failed. The owner's direction: "the smallest
00007| possible tasks you encounter on the way must be fully supported by it".
00008| 
00009| ## How the tasks were run
00010| 
00011| - **Client-level (the real thing).** `node js/server/main.mjs --port 18931
00012|   --agent-mode` with `FORMAL_AI_MEMORY_PATH` in a throwaway directory, and the
00013|   link-assistant Agent CLI 0.26 (`agent run --prompt … --model
00014|   formal-ai/formal-ai`) with an `opencode.json` provider block pointing at
00015|   `http://127.0.0.1:18931/v1`. Each task runs in a new git sandbox, so the
00016|   resulting `git diff` is the outcome.
00017| - **In-process (the inner loop).** `node experiments/js_dogfood/drive.mjs
00018|   --dir <sandbox> "<prompt>"` runs the same planner the server runs
00019|   (`planChatStep`) and executes each tool call on the sandbox with the Agent
00020|   CLI's result shapes. A run takes about a second instead of a CLI session.
00021|   Every fix is reproduced here first and then confirmed through the CLI.
00022| - **Regression tests.** `rust/tests/web/pull-request-1188-dogfood.test.mjs`
00023|   replays each fixed task with the Agent CLI's tool names and result formats
00024|   over an in-memory workspace, and asserts the exact file content and the
00025|   exact answer.
00026| 
00027| ## Ladder
00028| 
00029| | # | Task (prompt) | Before | After |
00030| | --- | --- | --- | --- |
00031| | T1 | `Add a function multiply(a, b) to math.mjs that returns a times b, add a test for it to math.test.mjs, and run node --test to confirm it passes.` | **Fail, destructive**: `math.mjs` was overwritten with the text `a function multiply(a, b)`; a plan file was written under `.formal-ai/`; the answer said the change was complete. | **Pass end-to-end through the CLI** (round 4): read both → write `math.mjs` (keeps `add`, adds `export function multiply(a, b) { return a * b; }`) → write `math.test.mjs` (`{ add, multiply }`, `assert.equal(multiply(2, 3), 6)`) → `node --check math.mjs` → `node --test` (2 pass). |
00032| | T2 | `Create a file a.txt containing hello` | Pass: `a.txt` = `hello`. | — |
00033| | T3 | `Read the file math.mjs and tell me its first line.` | Pass: answered with the first line. | — |
00034| | T4 | `Append the line 'third line' to notes.txt.` | **Fail, destructive**: `notes.txt` was overwritten with `the line 'third line'`. | **Pass**: read → edit → `sha256sum` check; one line added; answer `Appended \`third line\` to the end of \`notes.txt\` and observed the result.` |
00035| | T5 | `In greet.py rename the variable nmae to name.` | Pass: both occurrences renamed. | — |

00704| ## Root causes and fixes
00705| 
00706| ### T4 — an append was planned as a whole-file write
00707| 
00708| **Root cause.** No planner arm knew that a quoted payload can be placed at one
00709| end of an existing file. `Append the line '…' to notes.txt.` therefore reached
00710| the general-change fallback (`composeGeneralChangePlan`,
00711| `js/agentic/general_planner.mjs`), which reads any "verb + file + content"
00712| request as `literal_file` mode: write the content as the *whole* file. The
00713| content it extracted was the clause after the verb (`the line 'third line'`),
00714| not the quoted payload. Same mechanism as T1.
00715| 
00716| **Fix (general, seeded).**
00717| 
00718| - `data/seed/meanings-repository-workflow.lino` gains two position meanings,
00719|   `file_edit_position_end` and `file_edit_position_start`, next to the existing
00720|   `file_edit_position_after` / `_before`, each with en/ru/hi/zh/es surfaces
00721|   (`append`, `to the end of`, `в конец`, `追加`, `al final de`; `prepend`,
00722|   `at the top of`, `в начало`, `开头`, `al principio de`, …).
00723|   `data/seed/roles.lino` is regenerated by `scripts/generate-role-registry.py`.
00724| - `js/agentic/workspace_change.mjs` (the arm that already owns grounded
00725|   renames and replacements) gains an end insertion: the position from those
00726|   meanings, the payload from the request's one quoted segment that is not the
00727|   path, the target from the one workspace path. It reads the file, computes the
00728|   new content (a file without a final newline keeps none; a missing file is
00729|   created, as `>>` would), edits the smallest unique run of trailing (or
00730|   leading) lines, checks the result with `sha256sum`, and answers from the
00731|   seeded responses keyed by the same two meanings
00732|   (`data/seed/multilingual-responses-agentic-tools.lino`, five languages).
00733| - Because the arm runs before the general-change fallback, the fallback no
00734|   longer sees append requests.
00735| 
00736| **Test.** `rust/tests/web/pull-request-1188-dogfood.test.mjs`, "an append
00737| keeps the file it appends to": the exact T4 prompt and tool sequence
00738| (`read`, `edit`, `bash`), the exact file content and answer, no plan file;
00739| plus prepend, no-final-newline, missing-file and Russian variants.
00740| 
00741| **Rust twin.** Ported (see "Rust twin of the workspace-change fixes").
00742| 
00743| ### T7 — a replacement that contains its pattern was handed to a bare edit
00744| 
00745| **Root cause.** `groundedRewrite` (`js/agentic/workspace_change.mjs`) refused
00746| any substring replacement whose new text contains the old one, because the
00747| substring Markov rewrite would not terminate on `smal` → `small`. The request
00748| then fell to the intent-router edit, which sends the bare word as `oldString`
00749| — ambiguous whenever the word also sits inside a longer one.
00750| 
00751| **Fix.** A replacement of one word by another word containing it is
00752| word-scoped (the same scope a rename uses; the stated intent stays
00753| "replaced"). When the bare pattern is not unique in the file, the edit carries
00754| the smallest run of whole changed lines that is unique (`changedLinesEdit`);
00755| the result is checked by digest as before.
00756| 
00757| ### T8 — single-quoted literals were invisible to the positional insert
00758| 
00759| **Root cause.** `quotedLiterals` in `js/agentic/positional_edit.mjs` (and
00760| `quoted_literals` in `rust/src/agentic_coding/positional_edit.rs`) had its own
00761| scanner for `"` and `` ` `` only, while every other literal reader uses
00762| `quotedSegmentSpans`, which also reads `'…'` (with an apostrophe guard), «»,
00763| “”, 「」. The insert also ended in the generic tool-result answer, because only
00764| the intent-router edit handled it.
00765| 
00766| **Fix.** Both roots read literals through the shared `quoted_segment_spans`
00767| (Rust twin implemented). The JS workspace-change arm now owns positional
00768| inserts: the anchor must occur exactly once (otherwise the honest
00769| verification-failure answer, nothing written), the edit is checked by digest,
00770| and the answer comes from seeded responses keyed by the existing
00771| `file_edit_position_after` / `_before` meanings (five languages).
00772| 
00773| **Tests.** "a replacement edits only what it names" in
00774| `rust/tests/web/pull-request-1188-dogfood.test.mjs`: the T7 file, the T8
00775| prompt, and a twice-occurring anchor that must not be edited. The test's edit
00776| tool refuses an ambiguous `oldString` exactly as the Agent CLI does.
00777| 
00778| **Rust twin.** The quoting fix is in both roots; the rest is ported (see
00779| "Rust twin of the workspace-change fixes").

00781| ### T9 — no arm removed quoted text from a file
00782| 
00783| **Root cause.** Nothing in the seed bound "delete/remove" to *text in a file*:
00784| the only removal surfaces belonged to `cancel` (undo a program change) and to
00785| reserved-word lists. With no edit pair and no write content, the request fell
00786| through to the file-read arm, which showed the file.
00787| 
00788| **Fix.** A seeded action meaning `coding_text_remove` (role
00789| `coding_text_remove_action`; en/ru/hi/zh/es surfaces; `drop`/`erase` were left
00790| out because they are not grounded tokens yet) and a removal in the
00791| workspace-change arm: every line that is exactly the quoted payload goes,
00792| otherwise its single occurrence inside a line does; anything else is the
00793| honest verification-failure answer with nothing written. The end insertion and
00794| the removal now share one planner, `planComputedChangeStep` (read → compute
00795| bytes → smallest unique edit, else whole-file write → digest → seeded answer).
00796| `Delete the file notes.txt.` still plans `rm` — a quoted path is never a
00797| payload.
00798| 
00799| **Tests.** "a removal takes out what it quotes": the T9 prompt, an in-line
00800| removal, the file-deletion non-regression, and text found nowhere.

00802| **Whole JS suite.** `node --test --test-concurrency=1 rust/tests/web/`:
00803| 945 pass, 0 fail after T7–T9.

00805| **Rust twin.** Ported (see "Rust twin of the workspace-change fixes").

00807| ### T13 — the sentence's full stop was part of the command
00808| 
00809| **Root cause.** `prefixedShellCommand` (`js/agentic/shell_command.mjs`,
00810| `prefixed_shell_command` in Rust) took everything after the passthrough
00811| prefix (`run`, `execute`, …) verbatim, so the sentence's final `.` and any
00812| backticks around the command became shell text.
00813| 
00814| **Fix (both roots).** `trimCommandSentenceEnd` peels the outer quotes and the
00815| last token's sentence dot to a fixpoint, reusing `trimTrailingSentenceDot` —
00816| the path-token rule that keeps `.` and `..` intact — so `cd ..` and `ls .`
00817| are unchanged.
00818| 
00819| ### T14 — "directory" routed to a listing
00820| 
00821| **Root cause.** The named-capability router matched the word "directory" to
00822| `list_dir`. It already declined a read-many route for a request naming a
00823| *mutating* shell intent, but (a) the guard covered read-many only and (b) the
00824| `mkdir` intent declared no effect, so it did not count as mutating — effects
00825| could only be written for two-operand intents (`cp`, `mv`).
00826| 
00827| **Fix.** The guard covers every observing capability (`read_many`,
00828| `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`) in both roots. Effect expansion accepts one
00829| operand as `{path}` in both roots (`expand` / `expand_with`), and
00830| `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` declares the `mkdir` effect (`test ! -e
00831| {path}` before, `test -d {path}` after), so the request runs as a verified
00832| recipe. `rust/tests/unit/issue_680_intent_routing.rs` now expects the
00833| recipe's first step (`test ! -e build`) for "Create a directory called
00834| build".
00835| 
00836| ### T15 — commits: unrecognised phrasing, ignored message, unconditional push
00837| 
00838| **Root cause.** The `git_commit_request` surfaces had no "commit all"; the
00839| commit subject was always generated; and the plain-commit templates
00840| (`data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`) pushed to `origin` unconditionally, so a
00841| local repository's commit was reported through a push failure.
00842| 
00843| **Fix.** New surfaces ("commit all", "commit everything", "commit my
00844| changes"); a seeded concept `message` (role `git_commit_message_lead`, five
00845| languages) whose first following quoted segment becomes the subject
00846| (`statedSubject` / `stated_subject`, both roots); the two plain-commit
00847| templates push only `if test -n "$(git remote)"`. The work-item recipe commit
00848| is unchanged.
00849| 
00850| **Tests.** "shell requests run what they name": T13's command and answer,
00851| T14's recipe and answer, T15's exact command.
00852| 
00853| **Whole JS suite.** 1020 pass, 0 fail.

00855| ### T16 — a filler word inside a cue phrase broke the cue
00856| 
00857| **Root cause.** Shell-intent cues match as literal substrings of a requesting
00858| sentence, so `show me git status` never contained the seeded cue `show git
00859| status`, and the request fell to web search.

00861| **Fix (both roots).** A seeded `cue_fillers` list in
00862| `data/seed/shell-intents.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es: `me`, `the`, `please`, `мне`,
00863| `मुझे`, …) and `sentenceCarriesCue` / `sentence_carries_cue`: a cue matches
00864| the sentence as written or once both drop the fillers. The literal match is
00865| tried first, so every existing match is unchanged.

00867| ### T17 — "the value of KEY" was read as literal text
00868| 
00869| **Root cause.** The edit composer split the request into old `the value of
00870| "debug"` and new `true`; nothing knew that "the value of K" names the
00871| assignment of K in a configuration file.

00877| line assigning the key (`"k": v`, `k: v`, `k = v`) gets the value, in the

00895| ### T18 — a named source file did not name its language
00896| 
00897| **Root cause.** The program-contract route (`programContractAnswer`, which
00898| builds a write → compile → run → compare-output recipe) recognised the
00899| language only from words ("Python"), so `hello.py` named none; the request
00900| fell to the shared solver, which answered in chat with the rediscovered
00901| documentation example (`main.py`, `Hello, world!`) and no execution recipe.

00903| **Fix (both roots).** `namedSourceLanguage` / `named_source_language` in
00904| `js/agentic/crate/coding_program_contract.mjs` and
00905| `rust/src/coding/program_contract.rs`: a line that asks for printed output
00906| (`print_stdout`), carries a creation verb (`coding_request_verb`: write,
00907| create, implement, …) and names exactly one source file whose extension is
00908| the `save_as` extension of exactly one non-framework catalogued language
00909| takes that language. The catalog is the source, so every catalogued language
00910| (`.rs`, `.go`, `.kt`, `.R`, …) is covered. Without the creation verb
00911| (`Change greet.py so it prints "Hi"`) nothing is claimed — that is an edit.
00912| 
00913| **The unquoted output (round 4).** `prints Hello, World! and run it`
00914| names its output without quotes, and the clause splitter keeps the whole
00915| sentence as one clause. Reading "the words after *prints* up to *and*" as a
00916| literal would also read `prints the sum of a and b` as the literal `the sum
00917| of a`, so the output boundary needed a grounded rule, not a guess.
00918| 
00919| *Root cause.* `boundOutputLiterals` / `bound_output_literals` (the obligation
00920| graph's output binding, `js/agentic/crate/intent_formalization_obligations.mjs`,
00921| `rust/src/intent_formalization/obligations.rs`) bound quoted segments only,
00922| so `explicitStdout` was empty, the program contract declined, and the shared
00923| solver answered in chat with the documentation example.
00924| 
00925| *Fix (both roots).* A clause that quotes nothing is read by `unquotedOutput` /
00926| `unquoted_output`: the words after its first `print_stdout` word, up to the
00927| first seeded clause separator (`skill_procedure_clause_separator`: and, then,
00928| и, फिर, …) or through the first word that ends a sentence. They are bound only
00929| when they read as an utterance — they open with a capital (as a quotation
00930| does mid-sentence), contain no `statement_function_word` (the, of, for, …),
00931| and mention no `coding_structure` and no `program_task_alias` unless that
00932| alias is itself a `social_greeting` (the hello-world program *is* its text).
00933| Accepted: `Hello, World!`, `Привет, мир!`, `Hi` (beside a quoted `Bye`, in
00934| request order). Rejected: `the sum of a and b`, `Fibonacci numbers up to
00935| 100`, `FizzBuzz`, `FizzBuzz for 1 to 100`, `prime numbers below 50`, `the
00936| greeting!`.
